title: A rare de novo prenatal case of Down syndrome due to der(21;21)(q10;q10)
chief_complaint: 13-week gestational prenatal screening with elevated Down syndrome risk (1 in 40) and multiple fetal sonographic malformations
history: 32-year-old G2P1 pregnant woman at 13 weeks gestation
No family history of chromosomal abnormalities
labs: QF-PCR Devyser Compact v3: False negative normal Chromosome 21 locus profile (21H, 21C peak ratio 1:1)
Parental High-Resolution Peripheral Blood Karyotyping: 46,XX and 46,XY (Both parents normal in 30 metaphases)
imaging: Fetal Ultrasound (13 weeks): Increased NT (2.79mm), bilateral jugular lymphatic sacs, marked tricuspid regurgitation, single umbilical artery
cytogenetics: Prenatal FISH Probe: ish (D21S270/D21S1440/D21S341)x3 (Three chromosome 21 signals with 2 red signals on derivative chromosome)
final_diagnosis: Down Syndrome (Trisomy 21) secondary to de novo Homologous Robertsonian Translocation der(21;21)(q10;q10)
expected_followup: Parental karyotyping to differentiate de novo (1-10% recurrence risk) vs balanced parental carrier (100% recurrence risk)?
Karyotype and FISH confirmation following rapid QF-PCR false negative?
